currentContext.expansion: During FY26, Triveni Turbines expanded its manufacturing and service footprint across multiple geographies. TTAI's Houston (Texas) facility, launched in FY25, was upgraded in FY26 with advanced equipment to boost service capacity, enabling TTAI to operate as both an OEM and independent refurbishment provider. TTAPL established new-market presence in Kenya, Ghana and Mozambique (a geothermal renewable-energy project, utility-sector engagement, and delivery of reverse-engineered turbine rotor components respectively), and integrated TSE Engineering into Triveni Turbines Africa to strengthen operational synergies across sub-Saharan Africa. Domestically, the Company undertook expansion of manufacturing capacity in Bengaluru, adopted digitalised hydro testing for turbine casings and advanced laser hardening processes, and expanded assembly/testing facilities in North America and South Africa. In FY26 the Company launched TRI-ZEN, a Manufacturing and Supply Chain Transformation initiative (TTPS 2.0) integrating lean principles, digital technologies and performance management to build a scalable, digitally enabled production system, alongside expansion of its global sourcing footprint. Going forward, the Company plans further investment in high-precision infrastructure and expansion of its manufacturing footprint at Sompura to build a scalable, future-ready manufacturing base.

risks.note: Heightened geopolitical instability across key markets, most notably the Middle East, is expected to weigh on order finalisations; deferred customer purchasing decisions amid macro/geopolitical uncertainty may slow order inflow, drive an adverse product-mix shift, and impact near-term profitability.

Middle East logistics disruptions (container-freight-station congestion, delivery variability, higher landed costs) together with slower receivables collection are pressuring supply-chain continuity, despatch schedules and working capital, and threaten continuity of critical raw-material supply including industrial gases (casting/forging) and petroleum-based inputs.

Regional instability and travel restrictions in the Middle East have led to deferral of spares despatch schedules and service engagements, affecting the relatively higher-margin aftermarket revenue; order finalisations in the refinery-driven (API) segment may also face postponement in FY27.

Uncertainty around US import tariffs, alongside the time required to establish TTL's brand presence in that market, could compress margins on imported components and extend the breakeven timeline for the US business; input-cost inflation and foreign-exchange volatility present additional pressure on profitability.

risks.risk: Technology maturity and new product introduction
risks.note: Deployment of emerging, lower-maturity technologies across materials, aerodynamics, sealing and controls in turbomachinery design carries risk of performance shortfalls, design delays, or higher development costs; pending validation of the Company's next-generation product series also constrains near-term addressable market and competitive positioning.

risks.risk: Product reliability, quality and field performance
risks.note: Gaps in design, material selection or life analysis during development could, in adverse cases, lead to rotor or blade distress; the broader level of customer issues remains elevated, and any persistent gap between contractually committed and field-achieved turbine performance could affect acceptability with EPC contractors and repeat-order conversion.

TTL faces standard manufacturing, IoT, and operational technology (OT) cyber risks, including potential supply chain attacks, intellectual property theft, and ransomware, with the risk of malicious cyberattacks becoming more defined as industrial automation increases.

TTL undertakes complex engineering and project execution assignments including deployment of emerging technologies; delays from engineering challenges, customer dependencies, technology integration issues, supply chain constraints, or scope changes may result in cost overruns, liquidated damages, margin erosion and working capital pressures, with execution risk higher in first-of-a-kind projects and innovative energy transition applications.

one-line thesis: Lumpy but structurally compounding sub-100 MW turbine oligopolist riding a globally synchronized energy-capex cycle (data-center power, geothermal, API), with exports now 58% of revenue and an enquiry book that nearly doubled YoY — near-term margins range-bound ~25% EBITDA, optionality from CO2/LDES, ORC and US scale-up.

guidance (next quarter / fy27):
- Mgmt shies from explicit guidance; closing order book growth of ~9% cited as the **minimum** revenue growth anchor for FY27.
- FY27 again expected **H2 back-ended**; receivables may stay near current ~84-day level due to execution profile.
- Exports expected to exceed domestic in FY27.
- US subsidiary: FY26 was a full-year loss (~₹8 cr) despite a profitable Q4; FY27 targeted breakeven-to-positive; sustained profitability from FY28.
- Confident in bottom-line growth FY27 despite expected continued geopolitical disruption.
- **Verify next quarter (Q1 FY27):** order-book ≥9% revenue conversion; receivable normalization; US subsidiary turning profitable; API order resurgence (mgmt said Q1 already showing good API demand).
order book & pipeline:
- Closing OB ₹20.54 bn (+8% YoY), exports 51% of OB.
- Enquiry book nearly **doubled YoY**; product enquiry pipeline ~18 GW (vs ~9 GW LY).
- Geographic: India enquiry book ~7 GW (+100% YoY); North America ~3 GW (up ~1,000% off tiny base; now ~15%+ of enquiry book vs 1-2%); Turkey the only declining market.
- Data-center end-market = **>50% of enquiry book** (combined-cycle steam turbines, geothermal, SMR, renewables feeding DC power — not grid).
- Drivers: thermal power capacity addition, fixed-capital formation (steel & cement largest; also paper/pulp, sugar, IPPs, process cogen), API/downstream oil & gas resurgence on higher oil prices.
segment / subsidiary:
- **Core**: sub-100 MW steam turbines — product + aftermarket. Still "pretty much a steam turbine company" near-term; multi-product/solutions in medium-long term.
- **Aftermarket** = spares + service (tied to ~2-3yr-old installed base) + **refurbishment** (the real growth lever; strong traction in Africa). Q4 aftermarket dropped to ~25% of sales vs ~33% FY25, a key margin drag.
- **US subsidiary**: profitable Q4, full-year loss ~₹8 cr; aftermarket (fast turnaround) to drive FY27 revenue, product orders execute FY28.
- **API/drive turbines**: key profit & growth driver; FY26 below expectation (lost large orders from India-Pakistan conflict); targeted to revert to 10%+ of OB & revenue.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **Geothermal**: technically demanding; aftermarket + new product; large multi-year opportunity (SE Asia, US).
- **ORC (Organic Rankine Cycle)**: new product for low-temp waste-heat & geothermal; expected first wins FY27.
- **CO2 / subcritical long-duration energy storage**: NTPC strategic project; marginally profitable; awaiting plant stabilization & round-trip-efficiency data before articulating business model. Higher cost than pumped hydro currently; wants to be value-added player, not integrator.
- **MVR / heat pumps**: small, high-margin, a door-opener / integrated-solution enabler — stays small.
- **SMR / microreactors**: a few US enquiries; treated as standard steam-turbine solution (low nuclear specs); already a nuclear-space supplier.
margins & cost dynamics:
- FY26 EBITDA margin 24.2% — in line with ~25% mean; mgmt insists margins not structurally impaired.
- Q4 compression drivers: (1) low-margin strategic NTPC order (PBT ~3%, two-thirds billed in FY26); (2) aftermarket fell to 25% of sales; (3) ~₹8.5 cr M2M FX loss (to reverse). Margin lifts with more exports, more aftermarket, more spares within aftermarket.
- Raw-material inflation (copper/aluminium/steel) managed via long-term rate contracts, diversified supplier base, back-to-back ordering, partial pass-through. No margin threat seen.
- Wins are not price-driven (oligopolistic global market); currency depreciation seen as margin upside, not share lever.
capex / expansion:
- No specific capacity-capex figure disclosed; emphasis on R&D and new-product commercialization. ~7.5% of workforce in R&D, ~8%+ in engineering, ~35% in servicing.
- Plans to invest "significantly more" into AI to stay technologically ready for disruption.
capital allocation:
- Disciplined; maintains **negative working capital** on balance-sheet reporting dates (Mar 31 / Sep 30).
- No buyback/dividend/M&A discussed on call; reinvestment into R&D, US footprint and aftermarket capability.
risks & watch-items:
- Quarterly lumpiness — mgmt repeatedly directs investors to TTM / YoY view.
- Elevated receivables (84 days) and persistent H2 back-ending; FY27 receivables may stay high.
- Recurring M2M FX losses from rupee volatility / hedging policy.
- Geopolitics (India-Pakistan, US tariffs, West Asia conflict) delayed order finalisation; FY27 disruptions expected to persist.
- Export order inflow was flattish YoY (₹~1,200 cr) — conversion delays in markets beyond US; Turkey visibility declining.
- US conversion uncertain (water permitting slow for combined-cycle; weak brand vs global peers).
- CO2/LDES economics unproven vs pumped hydro/BESS in low-cost Indian market.
management quality / tone: - High candour: admits PAT decline, US subsidiary loss, NTPC low margin (~3% PBT), API miss; declines to give precise breakups it doesn't have. Frames year as "satisfactory" against severe external headwinds. Consistent multi-year messaging; confident but cautious on conversion timing. Strong technical depth across the bench (CEO/COO/CMO all contributed substantively).
non-obvious takeaways:
- Data centers are now the single largest demand theme (>50% of enquiry book) but via **steam-turbine bottoming of combined-cycle gas plants** + geothermal/SMR — an indirect, less-crowded AI-power exposure than gas turbines.
- US enquiry surge (~1,000%) is off a near-zero base; aftermarket (short cycle) monetizes first (FY27), product orders only FY28 — so US revenue inflection is FY28, not FY27.
- The "strategic" NTPC CO2/LDES order deliberately dragged FY26 margins — a paid R&D validation, not a profit centre yet.
- Africa refurbishment is quietly emerging as a sustainable, higher-margin aftermarket growth engine.
- API recovery already visible in Q1 FY27 on higher global oil prices (upstream + downstream), but not yet in projections — potential upside.
- CO2 technology partner (unnamed) reportedly has Google + Engie offtake and Alliant Energy US build — TRITURBINE more cautious than partner, flagging cost/efficiency execution risk.

- CO2 technology partner (unnamed) reportedly has Google + Engie offtake and Alliant Energy US build — TRITURBINE more cautious than partner, flagging cost/efficiency execution risk.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Triveni Turbines is a globally dominant leader in industrial heat and power solutions and decentralised, sustainable energy systems, ranked among the top two global players in steam turbines.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Triveni Turbines is a steam turbine OEM providing end-to-end steam turbine solutions up to 100 MW and manufacturing, refurbishment, retrofit and lifecycle services for turbines up to 1,000 MW across leading global OEM platforms, with an installed base of 6,000+ turbines serving 20+ industries across 80+ countries. It has evolved from a product-focussed manufacturer into a comprehensive solutions provider spanning engineering, manufacturing, commissioning and aftermarket lifecycle support, and is expanding into next-generation decarbonisation technologies such as CO2-based heat pumps/chillers and Organic Rankine Cycle (ORC) turbines.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- Triveni Energy Solutions Ltd. (TESL) — subsidiary: Incorporated in India; subsidiary since 28.05.2010
- Triveni Turbines Europe Pvt. Ltd. (TTE) — subsidiary: Incorporated in United Kingdom; subsidiary since 23.12.2014
- Triveni Turbines FZCO (TTF) (formerly Triveni Turbines DMCC) — subsidiary: Incorporated in Dubai, UAE; subsidiary since 31.03.2015
- Triveni Turbines Africa (Pty) Ltd (TTAPL) — subsidiary: Incorporated in South Africa; subsidiary since 13.07.2017; anchors the Company's presence in the African market
- TSE Engineering (Pty) Ltd (TSE) — subsidiary: Incorporated in South Africa; subsidiary since 01.03.2022
- Triveni Turbines Americas Inc (TTA/TTAI) — subsidiary: Incorporated in United States of America; subsidiary since 16.02.2024; Houston, Texas facility serving the Americas
- Triveni Sports Private Limited — JV: Joint venture associated/acquired June 6, 2023; 50% equity holding with significant influence via board representation and management participation; equity-accounted, not consolidated

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary
segment_detail.body:
- **Core**: sub-100 MW steam turbines — product + aftermarket. Still "pretty much a steam turbine company" near-term; multi-product/solutions in medium-long term.
- **Aftermarket** = spares + service (tied to ~2-3yr-old installed base) + **refurbishment** (the real growth lever; strong traction in Africa). Q4 aftermarket dropped to ~25% of sales vs ~33% FY25, a key margin drag.
- **US subsidiary**: profitable Q4, full-year loss ~₹8 cr; aftermarket (fast turnaround) to drive FY27 revenue, product orders execute FY28.
- **API/drive turbines**: key profit & growth driver; FY26 below expectation (lost large orders from India-Pakistan conflict); targeted to revert to 10%+ of OB & revenue.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Steam Turbines (OEM):** Steam turbines up to 100 MW, Turbine manufacturing, refurbishment, retrofit and lifecycle solutions for turbines up to 1,000 MW
- **Aftermarket / Services:** Servicing, operations and maintenance of steam turbines (REFURB™), Spares supply, overhauling, refurbishment and performance enhancement
- **Next-generation / Energy transition:** CO2-based heat pumps and chillers, Organic Rankine Cycle (ORC) turbines, High Temperature CO2 Heat Pumps and CO2-based Energy Storage Systems (ESS)

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body:
- Closing OB ₹20.54 bn (+8% YoY), exports 51% of OB.
- Enquiry book nearly **doubled YoY**; product enquiry pipeline ~18 GW (vs ~9 GW LY).
- Geographic: India enquiry book ~7 GW (+100% YoY); North America ~3 GW (up ~1,000% off tiny base; now ~15%+ of enquiry book vs 1-2%); Turkey the only declining market.
- Data-center end-market = **>50% of enquiry book** (combined-cycle steam turbines, geothermal, SMR, renewables feeding DC power — not grid).
- Drivers: thermal power capacity addition, fixed-capital formation (steel & cement largest; also paper/pulp, sugar, IPPs, process cogen), API/downstream oil & gas resurgence on higher oil prices.

guidance.title: Guidance (next quarter / FY27)
guidance.body:
- Mgmt shies from explicit guidance; closing order book growth of ~9% cited as the **minimum** revenue growth anchor for FY27.
- FY27 again expected **H2 back-ended**; receivables may stay near current ~84-day level due to execution profile.
- Exports expected to exceed domestic in FY27.
- US subsidiary: FY26 was a full-year loss (~₹8 cr) despite a profitable Q4; FY27 targeted breakeven-to-positive; sustained profitability from FY28.
- Confident in bottom-line growth FY27 despite expected continued geopolitical disruption.
- **Verify next quarter (Q1 FY27):** order-book ≥9% revenue conversion; receivable normalization; US subsidiary turning profitable; API order resurgence (mgmt said Q1 already showing good API demand).

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body:
- **Geothermal**: technically demanding; aftermarket + new product; large multi-year opportunity (SE Asia, US).
- **ORC (Organic Rankine Cycle)**: new product for low-temp waste-heat & geothermal; expected first wins FY27.
- **CO2 / subcritical long-duration energy storage**: NTPC strategic project; marginally profitable; awaiting plant stabilization & round-trip-efficiency data before articulating business model. Higher cost than pumped hydro currently; wants to be value-added player, not integrator.
- **MVR / heat pumps**: small, high-margin, a door-opener / integrated-solution enabler — stays small.
- **SMR / microreactors**: a few US enquiries; treated as standard steam-turbine solution (low nuclear specs); already a nuclear-space supplier.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Global energy demand rising on industrialisation, AI/data-centre and digital-infrastructure growth, and accelerating electrification; global electricity demand growing at ~6% annually
- Structural shift toward renewable thermal solutions (biomass, waste-to-energy, waste heat recovery) alongside continued growth in conventional thermal capacity, as renewables alone cannot meet incremental demand
- India's energy transition driven by robust economic growth, industrialisation and urbanisation, with renewable capacity trajectory toward 500 GW by 2030
- Aftermarket business growth driven by the scale of the installed base, particularly the large installed base in the US, presenting refurbish/repair/modernise/upgrade opportunities
- North American enquiries surged multi-fold in FY26, driven by demand for AI data centres, small modular/nuclear reactors, and combined-cycle units
- Export growth momentum sustained across Southeast Asia, Europe and the Middle East despite geopolitical tensions and tariff barriers delaying some international order finalisations
- Shift in order-booking mix toward thermal renewable fuels — approximately 65% of FY26 order bookings were linked to sustainable/clean-energy applications
- Geopolitical disruptions (India-Pakistan conflict early in the year, West Asia crisis toward year-end, tariff uncertainty) affected order booking and execution timelines, but diversified geographic/sectoral presence supported resilience
- New product introductions (India's first Transcritical CO2-based heat pump, Mechanical Vapor Recompression systems) expected to deepen customer engagement and unlock incremental medium-to-long-term growth, though market uptake will be gradual
- USA subsidiary (TTAI, Houston) viewed as a key long-term growth market, with demand seen across data-centre thermal/combined-cycle applications, geothermal, biomass and pulp & paper
- Order booking remained resilient at ₹23,256 million (₹23.26 billion) in FY26, supported by robust demand and strong Q4 booking momentum
- Company closed FY26 with a healthy order book of ₹20,539 million, up 8% year-on-year, providing strong revenue visibility
- Enquiry pipeline more than doubled over the previous year (over March 2025), providing strong visibility for future growth
- Aftermarket order booking share increased to 38% of total orders in FY26, up from 26% in FY25
- Aftermarket order bookings surged 41% year-on-year to ₹8.78 billion; within this, REFURB™ order bookings surged 107% year-on-year, primarily driven by international finalisations
- Product business contributed ₹14.47 billion, accounting for 62% of total order bookings during the year; domestic order book grew 8% year-on-year
- Export order booking accounted for 52% of total orders in FY26, reflecting continued traction in Southeast Asia and Europe
- North American enquiries surged multi-fold during FY26, though tariffs and geopolitical unrest delayed order finalisation toward year-end

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body:
- FY26 EBITDA margin 24.2% — in line with ~25% mean; mgmt insists margins not structurally impaired.
- Q4 compression drivers: (1) low-margin strategic NTPC order (PBT ~3%, two-thirds billed in FY26); (2) aftermarket fell to 25% of sales; (3) ~₹8.5 cr M2M FX loss (to reverse). Margin lifts with more exports, more aftermarket, more spares within aftermarket.
- Raw-material inflation (copper/aluminium/steel) managed via long-term rate contracts, diversified supplier base, back-to-back ordering, partial pass-through. No margin threat seen.
- Wins are not price-driven (oligopolistic global market); currency depreciation seen as margin upside, not share lever.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Disciplined; maintains **negative working capital** on balance-sheet reporting dates (Mar 31 / Sep 30).
- No buyback/dividend/M&A discussed on call; reinvestment into R&D, US footprint and aftermarket capability.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: During FY26, Triveni Turbines expanded its manufacturing and service footprint across multiple geographies. TTAI's Houston (Texas) facility, launched in FY25, was upgraded in FY26 with advanced equipment to boost service capacity, enabling TTAI to operate as both an OEM and independent refurbishment provider. TTAPL established new-market presence in Kenya, Ghana and Mozambique (a geothermal renewable-energy project, utility-sector engagement, and delivery of reverse-engineered turbine rotor components respectively), and integrated TSE Engineering into Triveni Turbines Africa to strengthen operational synergies across sub-Saharan Africa. Domestically, the Company undertook expansion of manufacturing capacity in Bengaluru, adopted digitalised hydro testing for turbine casings and advanced laser hardening processes, and expanded assembly/testing facilities in North America and South Africa. In FY26 the Company launched TRI-ZEN, a Manufacturing and Supply Chain Transformation initiative (TTPS 2.0) integrating lean principles, digital technologies and performance management to build a scalable, digitally enabled production system, alongside expansion of its global sourcing footprint. Going forward, the Company plans further investment in high-precision infrastructure and expansion of its manufacturing footprint at Sompura to build a scalable, future-ready manufacturing base.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: - High candour: admits PAT decline, US subsidiary loss, NTPC low margin (~3% PBT), API miss; declines to give precise breakups it doesn't have. Frames year as "satisfactory" against severe external headwinds. Consistent multi-year messaging; confident but cautious on conversion timing. Strong technical depth across the bench (CEO/COO/CMO all contributed substantively).

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Ranked among the top two global players in a technically demanding steam turbine market traditionally dominated by large multinationals
- Strong leadership position in thermal renewable-fuel-based segments including biomass, Waste-to-Energy (WtE) and Waste Heat Recovery (WHR)
- Installed base of 6,000+ turbine installations serving 20+ industries across 80+ countries
- Deep expertise in thermodynamics, rotating equipment and system integration, backed by in-house R&D and collaborations with leading global and domestic institutions
- Global service network via Triveni Turbines Americas Inc. (TTAI) and Triveni Turbines Africa (Pty) Ltd (TTAPL) strengthening aftermarket support and lifecycle performance
- Growing export orientation (exports contributed 53% of BRSR-reported turnover and 58% of FY26 revenue) supported by a resilient domestic supply chain

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body:
- Quarterly lumpiness — mgmt repeatedly directs investors to TTM / YoY view.
- Elevated receivables (84 days) and persistent H2 back-ending; FY27 receivables may stay high.
- Recurring M2M FX losses from rupee volatility / hedging policy.
- Geopolitics (India-Pakistan, US tariffs, West Asia conflict) delayed order finalisation; FY27 disruptions expected to persist.
- Export order inflow was flattish YoY (₹~1,200 cr) — conversion delays in markets beyond US; Turkey visibility declining.
- US conversion uncertain (water permitting slow for combined-cycle; weak brand vs global peers).
- CO2/LDES economics unproven vs pumped hydro/BESS in low-cost Indian market.

qoq_log.title: QoQ change log
qoq_log.body: - First summary in this series for TRITURBINE — no prior quarter on file to diff against. Baseline established at Q4/FY26: record revenue (Q4 ₹6.8 bn, FY ₹21.81 bn), EBITDA margin 24.2%, OB ₹20.54 bn (+8%), exports 58% of revenue, enquiry book ~doubled YoY, US/CO2-LDES/geothermal/ORC as forward optionality. other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Macro risk] Management flags a named geopolitical exposure: "the evolving macroeconomic situation, particularly geopolitical uncertainties in the West Asia region, may cause near-term fluctuations", offset by "our diversity across geographies and segments".
- [Guidance] Management states "confidence to sustain year on year business growth and margin recovery in the latter half of FY27", having described Q1 FY27 margins as impacted by "an unfavorable mix, price escalation, and the delivery phasing of some strategic orders".
- [Market data] The overall global steam turbine market "Expanded at a Robust 17.7% CAGR During 2021-2025", from "60 GW in 2021 to 116 GW in 2025" (Source: McCoy Report 2025) — but the deck's own segment charts attribute that growth to the >100 MW band, not the company's <100 MW band.
- [Demand pipeline] The named enquiry pipeline is "international demand across oil & gas, biomass, waste-to-energy, utility, geothermal, and process co-generation segments, and a domestic base across steel, cement, sugar, and distillery".
- [Shareholding] Promoter holding is unchanged at 55.84% in both Jun-25 and Jun-26; the remaining FII/DII/Resident Individual/Others percentages are printed as an unlabelled block in the extraction and are not assigned here.
